name: app/tier-status
title: TierStatus
summary: Where an account stands on the verification ladder: the current rung, the ladder as an ordered list with each rung's state in words, the attestations held as facts, and what the next rung needs with a link to submit evidence. It takes data and computes no access decision.

props.name: attestations
props.description: Facts the account holds, in words ("Business registration checked"), with an optional detail (where or when).

props.name: requirements
props.description: What the next rung needs, in words, as the server decided it.

props.name: action
props.description: A link to submit evidence for the next rung.

props.name: tierLabels
props.description: Rename tiers in the app's words or another language.

props.name: copy
props.type: { current?: string; ladder?: string; held?: string; none?: string; next?: string; top?: string; done?: string; here?: string; upcoming?: string }
props.description: The panel's other words, for another language: "Current level:", the ladder's name, "What you hold", "No attestations yet.", "Next:", "This is the highest level.", and the rung states "Done", "Current", "Next".

props.name: id
props.description: The id the heading (`<id>-title`) is built from.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading's level; the two sections take the next level.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the root, merged last.

behaviour: A <section> labelled by its heading. Beside the heading, the current rung's glyph on its --tier-* container pair (decorative), and "Current level: <name>" in the tier's text colour.

The ladder is an <ol> of the five rungs, lowest first, each with its level number (decorative), its name, and its state in words: "Done" below the current rung, "Current" on it (aria-current="step", a muted fill), "Next" on the one above, nothing further up. Reached rungs wear their tier's container pair; the others an outline.
"What you hold" lists the attestations as facts with a check glyph, or says "No attestations yet.".
"Next: <name>" lists `requirements` and, with `action`, a link to submit evidence. At the top rung it says "This is the highest level." instead.
It computes no access decision and no score: the tier, the attestations and the requirements are given by the server (api-gateway `assurance.py` decides access).

default.description: A business at Contact Verified, working towards Government Verified.

unverified.description: No rung reached and nothing held.

keyboard: The evidence link, when there is one.
aria: Glyphs and level numbers are aria-hidden; every state is also written.

theming.brandOverlay: The evidence link is the shell's primary action (`--app-accent`, else `--primary`). Tier colours are their --tier-* roles in every brand.

responsive: Fills its container; rung names wrap rather than push their state out.
contract:
contract
  slot is "tier-status"
  when default shows strong "Contact Verified"
  when default shows h2 "Verification"
  when default shows h3 "Next: Government Verified"
  when default shows a "Submit documents"
  when unverified shows h3 "Verification"
  when top shows p "This is the highest level."
  when localised shows strong "Imethibitishwa na jamii"
end

checks.say: The panel is a section labelled by its heading.
The ladder is an ordered list of five rungs, named.
The current rung is marked as the current step.
Each rung's state is written: two done, one current, one next.
Rungs below are written Done.
The rung above is written Next.
A reached rung wears its tier's container pair.
A rung not reached is an outline.
The current tier's glyph is on its container pair.
The current level's name is in the tier's text colour.
Attestations are listed as facts.
Requirements for the next rung are listed.
The evidence link.
Nothing held says so.
Unverified has no rung reached: one current, one next, none done.
Unverified shows the shield on the neutral pair.
headingLevel 3 puts the sections at h4.
At the top there is no next rung and no link.
Rung states can be renamed.
The next rung can be renamed.
No script.
